name: embarch-chat
description: The owner's own Claude Code chat, beside the code: every thread of the window's desk at a glance, each chat on its work item, plus the embarch-ui launcher.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: It runs `claude` and reads the desk's token; a workspace must be trusted first.

embarch-mark.description: The EmbArch mark, in one colour

embarchChat.claudePath.description: The `claude` each chat runs. Defaults to the one on PATH, as the desk and terminals use (decision 30). User or Remote settings only — a workspace cannot set it.

embarchChat.idleMinutes.description: A chat's process closes this long after its last input or reply, unless a background task runs or it waits on you; the next message resumes it (decision 41). User or Remote settings only — a workspace cannot set it.

embarchChat.deskUrl.description: The embarch-desk service, on this machine only: a loopback address (127.0.0.1, ::1 or localhost); the extension refuses any other host and never sends the token to one. Only the extension's Node side calls it; the webview never holds the token. User or Remote settings only — a workspace cannot set it.

embarchChat.deskTokenPath.description: The desk's bearer token file. User or Remote settings only — a workspace cannot set it.

embarchChat.assistant.description: The Haiku assistant at the input: ghost text, the 💡 cards, reply chips and naming each chat (one stripped `claude -p --model haiku` call each, about $0.002). Off, only the CLI's own suggestion and the instant prefix match over your past prompts remain. User or Remote settings only — a workspace cannot turn it on.

embarchChat.showMessageTimestamps.description: Show the time above each of your messages and Claude's replies, to the second, with a date line where the day changes — to line a turn up against a serial log or a trace (decision 68). User or Remote settings only.

embarchChat.autosave.description: Before Claude reads, edits or writes a file, save that file's unsaved changes in the editor, as Claude Code's own panel does (decision 61). Off, Claude works on the copy on disk. User or Remote settings only — a workspace cannot set it.

embarchChat.continueAfterReload.description: After the window reloads, a chat that was mid-turn continues the step the reload interrupted, as Claude Code's own panel does (decision 63). Off, it comes back saying no reply follows. Either way this window's chats come back after a reload, never after a close. User or Remote settings only — a workspace cannot set it.

embarchChat.diagnosticsTool.description: Give Claude a getDiagnostics tool that reads VS Code's Problems panel, unsaved edits included — Claude Code's own IDE tool, served by this extension over the chat's stdio (decision 65). Off by default; on, its definition rides in every chat's tool list. Takes effect when a chat's process next starts. User or Remote settings only — a workspace cannot turn it on.

embarchChat.attachOpenFile.description: Add the file open in the editor to your messages, shown as a chip under the input with an × (decision 60, as Claude Code's claudeCode.attachOpenFile). Off, a file goes only with lines you select. User or Remote settings only.

embarchChat.attachSelection.description: Add the lines you select in the editor, with their text, to your messages, shown as a chip under the input with an × (decision 60, as Claude Code's claudeCode.attachSelection). Off, @ still inserts the selected lines. User or Remote settings only.

embarchUi.binaryPath.description: Path to the embarch-ui binary. Defaults to 'embarch-ui' on PATH — set an absolute path if it isn't installed there.

embarchUi.host.description: Host embarch-ui binds to. Must match embarch-ui's own BIND_ADDR (127.0.0.1 by default, loopback-only).

embarchUi.port.description: Port embarch-ui binds to. Must match embarch-ui's own BIND_PORT.

embarchUi.configPath.description: Optional path to an embarch-ui TOML config file. Sets EMBARCH_UI_CONFIG for the spawned process; left empty, embarch-ui's own zero-config defaults apply.

embarchUi.autoStart.description: Start embarch-ui automatically when VS Code starts (and stop it when VS Code closes).

scripts.test: node build.mjs && node build.mjs --tests && node --test test/*.test.mjs
